questions.q: What are the three buckets this lesson gives for triaging presentation feedback?
options: Fix before calling this done, log as technical debt, out of scope
Urgent, important, trivial
Business, technical, operational
Accept, reject, escalate
questions.explain: The lesson sorts feedback into fix-before-done (genuine gaps), log-as-technical-debt (acceptable, already-named limitations), and out-of-scope (good ideas for a future project).

questions.q: Per this lesson, why is treating every piece of feedback as equally urgent a problem?
options: It isn't a problem; all feedback should always be treated equally
It violates Salesforce's terms of service
It's how a finished capstone never actually finishes -- while treating everything as optional is how real gaps get waved away
It only applies to feedback from Priya, not Renata or Dmitri
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly names both failure modes: treating everything as urgent prevents completion, while treating everything as optional lets real gaps slide.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the five components of a "portfolio-ready" result from this capstone, per this lesson?
options: A notarized legal document
A paid Salesforce certification exam voucher
A separate, unrelated sample Apex project
The Git repository with real incremental commit history
questions.explain: The five components are the Git repository, the ERD and data dictionary, the five ADRs, a demo recording, and the retrospective -- the Git repository with real commit history is one of them.

questions.q: What does this lesson call this course's position on the Technical Architect ladder?
options: Capstone I, the very first milestone
Capstone II, the programmatic-development milestone between declarative Capstone I and advanced architecture coursework ahead
The final course in the entire ladder
An optional elective with no ladder position
questions.explain: The lesson places this course as Capstone II -- the programmatic milestone following declarative Capstone I and preceding advanced architecture coursework and the enterprise transformation capstone.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say the next course in the ladder assumes this capstone's skills are already solid rather than re-teaching them?
options: Because the next course covers a completely unrelated technology
Because this capstone's content will be deleted after this course
Because the enterprise transformation capstone ahead is built on the assumption that data modeling, security, Apex, LWC, and integration skills from this capstone are already in place
Because the next course does not require any Salesforce knowledge at all
questions.explain: The lesson states the advanced architecture coursework and the enterprise transformation capstone assume this capstone's technical core is solid, which is exactly why the portfolio-ready checklist matters beyond just an interview.
